column3: On what date did Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 (the EU AI Act) enter into force?
column5: 1 August 2024.

column3: From what date do the prohibitions on AI practices in Article 5 of the EU AI Act apply?
column5: From 2 August 2025.

column3: Above what cumulative amount of compute used for training is a general-purpose AI model presumed to present systemic risk?
column5: More than 10^25 FLOPs of cumulative compute used for its training.

column3: What is the maximum fine for violating a prohibited AI practice under Article 5 of the EU AI Act?
column5: Up to EUR 35,000,000 or, if the offender is a company, up to 7% of its total worldwide annual turnover, whichever is higher.

column3: What is the maximum fine for violations of the EU AI Act other than Article 5 prohibited practices and supplying incorrect information to notified bodies?
column5: Up to EUR 15,000,000 or, if the offender is a company, up to 3% of its total worldwide annual turnover, whichever is higher.

column3: How many distinct prohibited AI practices are listed in Article 5(1) of the EU AI Act?
column5: Eight.

column3: Is social scoring of individuals under the EU AI Act prohibited or merely treated as a high-risk practice?
column5: Prohibited under Article 5(1)(c), for both public and private actors.

column3: In which annex of the EU AI Act are the categories of high-risk AI systems listed?
column4: Art 6(2) and Annex III of Regulation (EU) 2024/1689
column5: Annex III.

column3: What is the maximum fine for supplying incorrect, incomplete or misleading information to notified bodies under the EU AI Act?
column5: Up to EUR 7,500,000 or, if the offender is a company, up to 1% of its total worldwide annual turnover, whichever is higher.

column3: Is it prohibited to put on the market or put into service AI systems that infer emotions of natural persons in the workplace and in educational institutions?
column5: Yes, prohibited under Article 5(1)(f), except for narrow medical or safety reasons.

column3: Which provision of the EU AI Act prohibits the untargeted scraping of facial images from the internet or CCTV footage?
column5: Article 5(1)(e).

column3: Which provision of the EU AI Act prohibits AI systems used to evaluate or classify a person's risk of committing criminal offences based solely on profiling?
column5: Article 5(1)(d).

column3: Does the EU AI Act impose obligations on providers and deployers to take measures to ensure a sufficient level of AI literacy?
column5: Yes, to a reasonable extent and to the best of their ability, per Article 4.

column3: Under which article must AI systems intended to interact with natural persons be designed and developed so that those persons are informed that they are interacting with an AI system?
column5: Article 50(1).

column3: Under the EU AI Act, who must disclose that a deepfake has been artificially generated or manipulated?
column5: The deployer of the AI system that generated or manipulated the content.

column3: Under the EU AI Act, is a provider defined as a natural or legal person that develops an AI system or a general-purpose AI model and places it on the market or puts it into service under its own name or trademark?
column5: Yes.

column3: Does the EU AI Act define an AI system as a machine-based system designed to operate with varying levels of autonomy that infers how to generate outputs such as predictions, content, recommendations or decisions?
column5: Yes.

column3: If a high-risk AI system is substantially modified, must the provider carry out a new conformity assessment and update the technical documentation?
column5: Yes, a substantial modification triggers a new conformity assessment and requires updated technical documentation.

column3: Under which article must high-risk AI system providers establish, implement, document and maintain a risk management system?
column5: Article 9.

column3: Under which article must high-risk AI systems be designed and developed so that they can be effectively overseen by natural persons?
column5: Article 14.

column3: Do deployers of high-risk AI systems that are public entities or provide public services have to carry out a fundamental rights impact assessment before deploying the system?
column5: Yes, a fundamental rights impact assessment is required under Article 27.

column3: Must a high-risk AI system be CE marked before it is placed on the market or put into service in the EU?
column5: Yes, as part of the conformity assessment procedure, via Article 43.
